newsitem.title: USA: Polaroid net rises but stock falls.
newsitem.headline: Polaroid net rises but stock falls.

text.p: Polaroid Corp. said Thursday that earnings rose 21 percent in the second quarter, meeting expectations on Wall Street, but its stock fell as investors took profits after a recent run-up.

The world's largest maker of instant cameras and film said earnings from continuing operations rose to $34.5 million, or 76 cents a share, in the quarter ended June 29 from $28.5 million, or 63 cents a share, a year earlier. Results for the 1996 quarter excluded a one-time charge of about $55 million for restructuring debt.
The latest results were a penny above forecasts of 75 cents a share, according to First Call, which tracks analysts' estimates.
But Polaroid fell $1.125 to $55.125 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange after rising sharply in recent weeks as investors anticipated a good earnings report.
Sales fell 3 percent to $565 million from $582 million, as a rise of 6 percent in domestic sales was not enough to offset a drop in sales outside the United States.
"Overall, the second quarter met expectations," said company Chairman Gary DiCamillo. "We continue to realise the benefits from last year's restructuring and reductions of losses in digital imaging."
Sales of instant cameras rose for the eighth straight month in June, boosted by strong sales in Japan, and retail film sales rose modestly, he said.
Sales in Russia, where Cambridge, Mass.-based Polaroid has had major problems, remained weak. The company said it hired a new general manager in a bid to address problems there.
